mainTopic: Whether paying later for something forbidden counts as paying for the איסור, using the employer-and-workers ברייתא, followed by whether one may be paid to break barrels of יין נסך.
overview: The amud starts in the middle of a ברייתא about an employer who feeds his workers. If he hands them a coin, he is not responsible for what they buy. If he says 'go eat and I'll pay,' he must worry about שביעית, מעשר and יין נסך. The גמרא infers from this that paying a debt later still counts as paying for the forbidden item. רב חסדא first limits the ברייתא to a storekeeper who regularly gives credit, but that answer is challenged twice. רבא then rules that a debt not tied to specific money is not forbidden. To explain why the ברייתא still worries, רב פפא says the employer paid a דינר in advance, and רב אשי says he handed over the food himself. Each of them reads the ברייתא's wording to fit his case. A new question follows: may someone be paid to break barrels of יין נסך? רב נחמן allows it and blesses him. The גמרא begins bringing a ברייתא about hoeing in a field of כלאים as possible support, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Worker spends the employer's coin himself: no worry
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's first case ends: when the employer just hands the workers money to buy food, he need not worry about שביעית, מעשר or יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: (He need not be concerned) not about שביעית, not about מעשר, and not about יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא partway through. This line finishes its first case: the employer gave the workers a coin to buy food themselves, and he is not responsible for what they buy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coin is in the workers' hands, it is theirs. Whatever they buy, they buy on their own. So even if they spend it on forbidden food, the employer has done nothing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the seventh (שמיטה) year, which has special restrictions on how it may be traded
Tithe; produce from which the tithes were not taken may not be eaten
Wine poured for idol worship, which is forbidden to drink or benefit from

phrases.english: not because of Sabbatical-Year produce,
and not because of tithe,
and not because of libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיעִית, וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם מַעֲשֵׂר, וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that was quoted just before this section began.
steps.raayaObject: Whether paying later for a forbidden purchase counts as paying for the איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about an employer feeding his workers (first case).

steps.title: 'Go eat and I'll pay': the employer must worry
steps.stepSummary: Second case of the ברייתא: if the employer says 'go eat/drink and I will pay,' he must worry about שביעית, מעשר and יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said to them, 'Go and eat and I will pay,' or 'Go and drink and I will pay,' he must be concerned about שביעית, מעשר and יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case. Here the employer promises to pay the bill himself, so he is responsible if the workers eat forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference is who pays. When the employer settles the bill later, it is as if he bought the food and handed it to the workers. This is the line the גמרא will build its proof on.

keyTerms.meaning: Pays off, settles a debt
Must be concerned / take the איסור into account

phrases.english: But if he said to them:
'Go out and eat, and I will pay,'
'Go out and drink, and I will pay' —
he must be concerned about Sabbatical-Year produce,
and about tithe, and about libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וְאִכְלוּ וַאֲנִי פּוֹרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: paying the bill yourself makes you responsible.
steps.raayaObject: Whether paying later for a forbidden purchase counts as paying for the איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about an employer feeding his workers (second case).

steps.title: Inference: paying later is still paying for the איסור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that paying afterward counts as paying for the forbidden item. It applies this to the case it is discussing, borrowing שביעית produce and paying later.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that when he pays, he is paying the price of something forbidden. Here too, when one pays, he is paying the price of something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא and applies it to the case under discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The employer pays after the food is already eaten, yet the ברייתא still holds him responsible. So paying a debt later is treated as paying for the forbidden thing itself. The same should be true when someone borrows שביעית produce and pays for it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently / so we see (introduces an inference)
The price (money) of something forbidden
Here too (applying the lesson to our case)

phrases.english: Apparently, when he pays —
he is paying the price of a forbidden thing;
here too, when he pays —
he is paying the price of a forbidden thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, כִּי קָא פָרַע — דְּמֵי אִיסּוּר קָא פָרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא's second case.
steps.raayaObject: That paying a debt later for a forbidden item is treated as paying for the איסור, which applies to borrowed שביעית produce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that 'go eat and I'll pay' makes the employer responsible.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, anyone who borrows forbidden produce and pays for it later would be considered to have paid for the איסור.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the ברייתא is about a storekeeper who gives regular credit
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא is about a storekeeper who regularly gives the employer credit. The employer owes the debt the moment the food is handed over, so it does not prove anything about paying later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it as a storekeeper who gives him credit, so he becomes obligated to him. Since it is his regular way to give credit, the storekeeper acquires the דינר from him right then.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the proof by giving the ברייתא a narrower setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the employer's debt starts the moment the workers take the food, because the storekeeper always gives him credit. So it is as if the employer bought the forbidden food right then and gave it to them. That is different from a loan that is only paid off later, so the proof from step 3 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it (gave the source a specific setting)
A storekeeper who gives him credit
Becomes obligated, owes a debt

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does not argue with the ברייתא's ruling. He only shows that the employer's debt there begins immediately, so it cannot teach us about a debt that is paid off later.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tried to prove that paying later for a forbidden item counts as paying for the איסור. רב חסדא answers that in the ברייתא the debt already starts at the moment of purchase. His answer is challenged in steps 5-6, and רבא replaces it with a different explanation in step 7.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda interpreted it
as a storekeeper who gives him credit,
so that he becomes obligated to him,
phrases.notes: The employer owes the storekeeper right away, as soon as the workers take the food.

phrases.english: for since it is his way to give credit —
he acquires the dinar from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא, not the ruling of the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the employer's debt only begins when he pays later. In fact, with a storekeeper who regularly gives credit, the debt begins at the moment of purchase.

steps.title: If credit made the difference, the ברייתא should have said so in its own case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what happens with a storekeeper who does not give credit. If that is permitted, the ברייתא should have taught the split inside the 'go eat and I will pay' case, not in a separate dinar case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a storekeeper who doesn't give credit, is it allowed? If so, instead of teaching 'Go eat with this dinar, go drink with this dinar,' the ברייתא should have made the split inside its own case: 'When is this said? With a storekeeper who gives credit, because the employer becomes obligated to him. But with a storekeeper who doesn't give credit, it is allowed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer from step 4. If credit is the key, the ברייתא picked a strange way to show the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, 'I will pay' is forbidden only because the storekeeper regularly gives credit. That would mean 'I will pay' with a no-credit storekeeper is allowed. If so, the ברייתא could have shown the split within the same 'I will pay' case, using the wording 'במה דברים אמורים.' Since it switched to a whole new case (handing over a dinar), it seems credit is not the real point.

keyTerms.meaning: Storekeeper, shopkeeper
Gives him credit (lets him buy now and pay later)
Let it make the split and teach it within the same case
In what case are these words said? (a formula that limits a rule)
Becomes obligated, owes a debt

phrases.english: But a storekeeper who does not give him credit
what then, is it permitted?
If so,
instead of teaching "Go and eat with this dinar,"
phrases.notes: This is the first case of the ברייתא, from step 1, where the employer hands over money.

phrases.english: "Go and drink with this dinar,"
let it make the split and teach it within that very case:
In what case are these words said?
With a storekeeper who gives him credit,
since he becomes obligated to him,
but a storekeeper who does not give him credit
— it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the ברייתא is about a storekeeper who gives credit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If credit were the deciding factor, the ברייתא would have split the 'I will pay' case itself instead of moving to a different case.

steps.title: Even without regular credit the employer is obligated, as a guarantor is
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: even with a no-credit storekeeper, the employer becomes obligated when he sends the workers. רבא's rule says one who asks another to pay someone becomes obligated by the law of a guarantor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: with a storekeeper who doesn't give credit, isn't the employer obligated too? Didn't רבא say: if someone tells his friend, 'Give a מנה to so-and-so, and all my property will be yours,' the friend acquires the property by the law of a guarantor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second attack on רב חסדא. The difference between credit and no credit does not really exist, because the employer becomes obligated either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא taught that when you tell someone to give money to a third person, you become obligated to him for it, just like a guarantor (ערב). The same applies here: when the storekeeper gives food to the workers because the employer asked, the employer owes him right away. So רב חסדא's credit/no-credit split falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces a second challenge)
A sum of money (one hundred dinars)
So-and-so
My property
By the law of a guarantor: one who commits to pay for what another receives

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' who is obligated here is the employer, not the storekeeper. The storekeeper gives the food, and the employer ends up owing him.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
with a storekeeper who does not give him credit,
does he not become obligated?
phrases.notes: The employer is the one who becomes obligated to the storekeeper.

phrases.english: But didn't רבא say:
One who says to his friend
"Give a מנה to so-and-so
and all my property will be acquired by you,"
he acquires it by the law of a guarantor!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: חֶנְוָנִי שֶׁאֵין מַקִּיפוֹ מִי לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger challenge to רב חסדא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's assumption that a no-credit storekeeper creates no obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's guarantor rule, asking someone to give to another person makes you obligated to him. So the employer is obligated even without regular credit, and the split disappears.

steps.title: רבא: the debt is real, but since it is not tied to specific money, it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the credit split. In every case the employer becomes obligated, but because the debt is not attached to particular money, the arrangement is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It makes no difference whether he gives credit or doesn't. Even though the employer is obligated to him, since he does not designate his debt to specific money, it is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חסדא's answer fell apart, רבא gives a new reason why paying later is not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that the employer always becomes obligated. Even so, a general debt that is not linked to any specific money does not make the later payment count as paying for the forbidden item. So borrowing (like the שביעית produce case) and paying later is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference
Even though
Designates, sets aside for a specific purpose
Obligation, debt
Becomes forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Owing money is not the same as paying with specific money. A general debt that is not tied to particular coins does not make the payment forbidden, so borrowing and paying later is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why borrowing שביעית produce and paying later is permitted, which is the question the sugya started with in step 3.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
It makes no difference if he gives him credit,
and no difference if he does not give him credit;
even though he is obligated to him,
since he does not designate his obligation
phrases.notes: He means the debt is not tied to any particular money; it is just a general obligation.

phrases.english: — it is not forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לָא שְׁנָא מַקִּיפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected explanation with a new reason
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any commitment to pay creates a debt, but a debt not tied to specific money does not count as buying the forbidden item, so paying later is permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Credit or no credit makes no difference; a general debt that is not designated is not forbidden.

steps.title: Why is the ברייתא concerned at all?
steps.stepSummary: If, as רבא said, the employer's debt is not tied to specific money, why does the ברייתא say it is a concern because of שביעית?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why is the employer in the ברייתא worried about שביעית? He has not tied his debt to anything specific here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's conclusion by pointing to the ברייתא, which still says there is a worry about שביעית in the 'go eat and I will pay' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the arrangement is not forbidden because the debt is not attached to particular money. But the ברייתא clearly says 'I am concerned because of שביעית.' So something in the ברייתא's case must be different, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: is concerned; worries that something may be forbidden
the seventh year, whose produce may not be used for business
sets aside, designates for a specific purpose
a legal obligation or lien; a debt one owes

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכָא אַמַּאי חוֹשֵׁשׁ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיעִית?
phrases.english: But here, why is he concerned because of שביעית?
He does not tie his obligation to anything specific here!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא אַמַּאי חוֹשֵׁשׁ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's conclusion from Step 7 using the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that an employer's debt that is not tied to specific money is not forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no designated debt means no problem, the ברייתא should not worry about שביעית in the 'go eat and I will pay' case.

steps.title: רב פפא: the employer paid a דינר in advance
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא's case is one where the employer paid the storekeeper a דינר ahead of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is where he paid the storekeeper a דינר in advance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a special case where money was already given to the storekeeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the employer paid the storekeeper first, the food the workers take is bought with that specific money. Now the employer really is acquiring the שביעית produce and using it to pay his workers' wages, which is why the ברייתא is concerned.

keyTerms.meaning: gave in advance, paid ahead of time
a coin (a dinar)

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
For example, where he gave him a dinar in advance.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the storekeeper. The employer paid him before the workers came to take food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִקְדִּים לוֹ דִּינָר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: the ברייתא is about a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe a plain 'go eat and I will pay' case with no designated money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a case where a דינר was given in advance, so the food is tied to specific money.

steps.title: רב זביד: then the wording should be 'I will calculate'
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד argues that if the employer had already paid, the ברייתא should have said 'I will calculate,' not 'I will pay.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I said this teaching before רב זביד of נהרדעא. He said to me: If so, instead of teaching 'Go eat, go drink, and I will pay,' it should have taught 'Go eat, go drink, and I will calculate.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא reports that רב זביד challenged רב פפא's answer based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money was already given, the employer has nothing left to pay. He would only need to work out how much to subtract from the דינר. So the words 'I will pay' do not fit רב פפא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching or ruling
instead of teaching
pays, repays
calculates, keeps an account
he should have (said)

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב זְבִיד מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא,
phrases.english: I said this teaching before רב זביד of נהרדעא,
phrases.notes: 'This teaching' is רב פפא's answer about the דינר paid in advance.

phrases.english: He said to me: If so,

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּתָנֵי ״צְאוּ וְאִכְלוּ, צְאוּ וּשְׁתוּ, וַאֲנִי פּוֹרֵעַ״,
phrases.english: instead of teaching 'Go eat, go drink, and I will pay,'

phrases.aramaic: ״צְאוּ וְאִכְלוּ, צְאוּ וּשְׁתוּ, וַאֲנִי מְחַשֵּׁב״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have taught 'Go eat, go drink, and I will calculate'!
phrases.notes: He means: I will figure out how much to take off the דינר I already gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that a דינר was paid in advance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'I will pay' implies payment still to come, which does not fit a case where money was already given.

steps.title: רב כהנא: read the ברייתא as 'I will calculate'
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא accepts the point and changes the wording of the ברייתא to 'Go, and I will calculate.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Teach it as 'Go, and I will calculate.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב זביד by adjusting the ברייתא's wording to match רב פפא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of dropping רב פפא's answer, רב כהנא fixes the text of the ברייתא. With the new wording, the ברייתא clearly describes a case where money was paid first.

phrases.english: He said to him: Teach it as 'Go, and I will calculate.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב זביד's challenge from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's words 'I will pay' seemed to rule out a case of advance payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the ברייתא as 'I will calculate,' which fits advance payment.

steps.title: רב אשי: the employer handed over the food himself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the employer took the food from the storekeeper and handed it to the workers himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where he took the food and gave it with his own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to explain why the ברייתא is concerned about שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the employer himself takes the שביעית food and hands it to the workers, he is acquiring it and paying their wages with it directly. That is why the ברייתא worries, even without an advance דינר.

keyTerms.meaning: took
gave by hand, handed over personally

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
For example, where he took it and gave it by hand.
phrases.notes: The employer took the food from the storekeeper and handed it to the workers himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּטַל וְנָתַן בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of Step 8, in place of רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: a different specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The workers seemed to take the food from the storekeeper on their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The employer personally took and handed over the food, so he is paying with the forbidden produce.

steps.title: רב יימר: then the wording should be 'take and eat'
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר argues that if the employer handed the food over, the ברייתא should say 'take and eat,' not 'go and eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: If so, instead of teaching 'Go eat, go drink,' it should have taught 'Take and eat, take and drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר challenges רב אשי's answer based on the ברייתא's wording, just as רב זביד did to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Go and eat' suggests the workers go to the store on their own. If the employer is handing them the food, the natural words would be 'take and eat.'

keyTerms.meaning: take! (said to a group)
go out! (said to a group)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב יימר said to רב אשי:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּתָנֵי ״צְאוּ וְאִכְלוּ, צְאוּ וּשְׁתוּ״,
phrases.english: If so, instead of teaching 'Go eat, go drink,'
it should have taught 'Take and eat, take and drink'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading that the employer handed over the food himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'go and eat' describe workers going on their own, not receiving food from the employer's hand.

steps.title: רב אשי: read the ברייתא as 'take and eat'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי accepts the point and changes the ברייתא's wording to 'take and eat, take and drink.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Teach it as 'Take and eat, take and drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by adjusting the ברייתא's wording to fit his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like רב כהנא did earlier, רב אשי keeps his answer and corrects the text. Both answers now agree with רבא: there is only a problem when the food is tied to specific money or handed over directly.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule stands: sending workers to a storekeeper is normally fine. The ברייתא's worry about שביעית is limited to a case where the employer paid a דינר first (רב פפא) or handed over the food himself (רב אשי).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּנֵי ״טְלוּ וְאִכְלוּ, טְלוּ וּשְׁתוּ״.
phrases.english: He said to him: Teach it as 'Take and eat, take and drink.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יימר's challenge from Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'go and eat' seemed to rule out the employer handing over the food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the ברייתא as 'take and eat,' which fits the employer handing the food over.

steps.title: Wages for breaking barrels of יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: A group of חכמים ask whether a person may take wages for breaking barrels of יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן, עולא and אבימי בר פפי were sitting, and רבי חייא בר אמי was sitting with them, and they asked: If someone hired him to break barrels of יין נסך, what is the law? Do we say that since he wants the barrels to stay whole until then, his wage is forbidden? Or maybe anything done to reduce idol worship is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The חכמים raise a question about wages earned for destroying יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: the worker gains only if the wine exists to be broken, so he 'wants' it to stay, and getting benefit from it is forbidden. The other side: his work gets rid of something connected to idol worship, and that kind of work may be allowed. רב נחמן answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: wine poured or used for idol worship, forbidden to benefit from
to break
wants it to continue to exist
something shameful or improper; here, idol worship
it is fine, it is permitted
they were in doubt, they asked

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not about breaking the wine, which is clearly a good thing. The question is only whether he may take payment for doing it.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן וְעוּלָּא וַאֲבִימִי בַּר פַּפִּי,
phrases.english: רב נחמן and עולא and אבימי בר פפי were sitting,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי גַּבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and רבי חייא בר אמי was sitting with them,
and they were sitting and asking:
If one hired him to break barrels of יין נסך, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דְּרוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Do we say that since he wants it to stay in existence, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He wants the barrels to stay whole until he breaks them, since that is how he gets paid.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֹּל לְמַעוֹטֵי תִּיפְלָה שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps anything done to reduce idol worship is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about wages connected to forbidden items.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether wages earned for breaking barrels of יין נסך are permitted or forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Let him break the barrels and be blessed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers the question about breaking barrels of יין נסך for pay. He rules that the person may break them, and a blessing should come upon him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: He may break the barrels, and a blessing should come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question from step 15. He says the worker may go ahead and break the barrels of יין נסך, and he even deserves a blessing for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether getting paid for this work counts as benefiting from forbidden wine. רב נחמן treats breaking the barrels as a good act, since it destroys the forbidden wine. So the job is allowed, and the worker is praised for doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: He may break (the barrels)
And let a blessing come upon him
Wine poured or used for idol worship, forbidden for any benefit

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
He may break them, and let a blessing come upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 15 about taking wages for breaking barrels of יין נסך.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may be paid to break barrels of יין נסך.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes: he may break them, and he deserves a blessing for doing so.

steps.title: Proposed support from a teaching about hoeing in a field of mixed crops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא may support רב נחמן. It begins quoting it: one may not hoe together with a גוי in a field of כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? It teaches: One may not hoe together with a גוי in a field of כלאים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a possible proof for רב נחמן. It starts quoting a ברייתא about working with a גוי in a field of כלאים, and the rest of the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לֵימָא signals that this is only a suggested proof, and the גמרא may later reject it. The first part of the ברייתא says hoeing is forbidden, because hoeing helps the forbidden crops grow. The point of the comparison will become clear once the ברייתא is quoted in full.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (a source) supports him? This introduces a suggested proof.
Hoeing, loosening the soil around plants so they grow better
Forbidden mixtures of different kinds of plants grown together

steps.confusionAlert: לֵימָא does not mean the proof works. It only offers a possible proof, and the גמרא often pushes it away right after.

phrases.english: Let us say that a ברייתא supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב נחמן, who just allowed breaking the barrels.

phrases.english: One may not hoe together with a gentile in a field of diverse kinds,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible support from a ברייתא for רב נחמן's ruling in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that one may break barrels of יין נסך and be blessed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about hoeing with a גוי in a field of כלאים. Only its opening is quoted here.
